web_evidence.title: Sing, Unburied, Sing — Chapter 9 Extract
web_evidence.note: Authorized prize-site extract labels Chapter 9 “Richie” and sustains Richie's participating first-person narration across the chapter.

web_evidence.title: Subversive Ghosts: Rewriting Stories and Histories in American Women’s Ghost Literature
web_evidence.note: University-hosted dissertation explicitly states that the novel combines the first-person narrations of Jojo, Leonie, and Richie, while River’s first-person account is filtered through Jojo’s narrative.

web_evidence.title: Haunting Time in Jesmyn Ward’s Sing, Unburied, Sing
web_evidence.note: Scholarly analysis identifies Jojo, Leonie, and Richie as the three narrators, states that no omniscient narrator controls the novel, and describes each as telling part of the same story.

web_evidence.title: Sing, Unburied, Sing by Jesmyn Ward
web_evidence.note: Publishers Weekly’s unabridged-audio review independently identifies three narrators—Richie, Jojo, and Leonie—and three corresponding performers.

search_log: Searched “Sing Unburied Sing Jesmyn Ward excerpt publisher first chapter” and publisher-domain variants; found and opened the Women’s Prize Chapter 9 extract.
Searched “Sing Unburied Sing three narrators Jojo Leonie Richie point of view” and “first-person narrators”; found explicit whole-book descriptions and opened university-hosted scholarly sources.
Searched for author interviews and interior extracts; the PBS and Los Angeles Review of Books pages were discoverable but returned access errors when opened, so they were not used as evidence.
Opened the Publishers Weekly audiobook review to verify the whole-book three-narrator structure; generic summaries and search snippets were not treated as primary person evidence.
person_note: The novel’s controlling narration is shared by Jojo, Leonie, and Richie, but all three are participating first-person narrators, so multiple narrators do not make the result ALTERNATING. Numerous event quotes independently expose sustained “I,” “me,” “my,” and “we” narration across distinct characters, including Richie passages corroborated by the authorized Chapter 9 extract. The university-hosted dissertation explicitly confirms that all three principal narrations are first person and explains that Pop/River’s embedded first-person account is filtered through Jojo rather than forming a different base-person section. Dialogue, generic aphorisms, the epigraph, and the dedication were excluded from base-person inference. No credible evidence of sustained second- or third-person base narration was found.
